quests.title: A Particularly Particular Author

dialogue.t: Your deeds on Seirai Island have been reported to me by Miss Etsuko. You've done very well.
But back on topic, the Guild has received a commission of even greater difficulty than that which you accomplished on Seirai. I wonder if you'd be interested...

dialogue.sit: Even Fatui Harbingers fall before me.

dialogue.t: The person who commissioned this quest is a Miss Sumida. As for the details, it might be best for you to get them straight from her.
Well then, ad astra abyssosque! I await the completion of your next feat.
Ah, hello there. Might you be the illustrious {NICKNAME}?
And Paimon's the illustrious Paimon!
Alright then. So, tell me, have you ever "obtained the mightiest sword in the village"?

dialogue.sit: The Harbinger of Dawn counts, I guess?

dialogue.t: Yeah, didn't we get that sw{RUBY#[S]Triumphant Harbinger of Dawn that Points Towards Victory}ord from Kaeya that one time?
Hahah, that does sound very strong. Maybe even a bit too deliberately so. Still...
Have you led a life surrounded by beautiful men and ladies?

Well then, did you defeat a giant dragon not long after your story began? Or perhaps, did you get wrapped up in some crisis upon which the survival of a nation hung? Have you ever faced off against "an elite antagonistic force with a numbered ranking scheme"?

dialogue.sit: Well, I can't say I haven't...

dialogue.t: But hang on, what do you mean by "not long after your story began"?
Or are you, perhaps, in fact a traveler from "another world," just like the main character in "Flowers for Princess Fischl"?
Hmm, I can't feel that sense of "destiny" that a protagonist should have from you.
Y'know, when Katheryne said this was going to be harder, did she mean that communicating was gonna be harder?
Eh!? Wait! Don't go!
Katheryne told me so much about you, so I assumed that you'd be more like a light novel protagonist, you know?
But in truth, I suppose such people are hard to find...

My name's Sumida. As for my pen name... I haven't finished thinking about it yet. I've got plans to take part in this year's "This Novel Is Amazing!" As such, I need a reliable adventurer to help me make a trip to Tsurumi Island.

That's right. Now, the name of my novel is currently "The Chronicles of the Sea of Fog." The broad strokes of its plot are as such: a nameless young lady(young man) and her(his) adventures in a nation shrouded in perpetual fog.
Well, the plot details are currently still in the works. But my eventual goal is to write an epic novel that can move hearts and souls, like "Kino's Travels"!
Yup, it's that very same "Kino's Travels"!

In which an outlander named Kino who doesn't quite fit in anywhere strides across many strange lands. She meets all sorts of people, and she is drawn into all kinds of wicked plots and all manner of cruel wars. Yet each one of her adventures shall someday coalesce into shining gold...
Paimon doesn't quite get it, but it does sound like she's talking about you, {NICKNAME}...
Ah, right. Sorry, I got off topic.
Actually, I've been reflecting on that habit of mine quite often. It seeps into my writing as well, to the point where I once wrote over 20 pages before ever getting to the point.

At that time, I wanted to use the legend of the Kitsune Saiguu ushering people into the underground halls of Araumi to save them from a disaster as the basis for a tale about her new incarnation's peaceful life amongst the people of Hanamizaka...

dialogue.sit: So what do you need me to do on Tsurumi Island?

dialogue.t: My bad, my bad... So, please go to Tsurumi Island and find a way to bring a Maushiro back to me. This is a traditional instrument of the civilization native to the island, which has been lost for several millennia now.

As to why I need one, the — fictional, obviously — plot of "The Chronicles of the Sea of Fog (Working Title)" takes place on Tsurumi Island, and when a nameless young lady(young man) sets foot upon it—
Let's go, {NICKNAME}.
—They hear a strange sound but it's actually the sound of the traditional Maushiro recording in folktales so please I want to properly describe its sound and that's why I need a real Maushiro!

Nah, she was almost about to go off on some tangent or another. Still, do you really need a real Maushiro just to write a novel, Miss Sumida? Wouldn't a "dududu" or a "phweeet" do just fine if you needed to describe the sound it makes?
Writing is a most serious endeavor. You must treat the things you are describing with the utmost respect.
For example, if you wish to describe Balethunder, you must go to Musoujin Gorge to experience it! That's the only way you can maintain authenticity and credibility!
True, and I almost died back then, too. If I hadn't instructed Kama to get me out of there if he saw that something was going awry...
I was laid up in bed for a few days after that rescue. Everything I could see, everything I threw up... It was all purple.
But now that I think about it, the fact that everything I threw up was purple might've been a result of my only being able to see in purple at the time.

dialogue.sit: Sounds more like you had too much Lavender Melon to eat.
And what did you get written?

dialogue.t: Huh. Now that you mention it, that's true. I should compare and contrast the two experiences next time.
In any case, this letter is for you. Pass it to a man named Kama in Ritou, and he will take you to Tsurumi Island.
Please, this year's "This Novel is Amazing!" grand prize is at stake!
Ah, hello there. Might you be the illustrious {NICKNAME}?
And Paimon's the illustrious Paimon!
Alright then. So, tell me, have you ever "obtained the mightiest sword in the village"?
Have you led a life surrounded by beautiful men and ladies?

Please, this year's "This Novel is Amazing!" grand prize is at stake!
What is it?
Another one, huh?
...It's nothing. Since Lady Sumida has recommended you, I have no complaints. Are you ready to go to Tsurumi Island?
Then let us go while the weather remains clement.
Are you ready?
Then let us go while the weather remains clement.
You're back. Do you have the Maushiro?

dialogue.sit: Could I ask about Kama for a moment?

dialogue.t: Him? ...Well, it all started when I heard Tang Wen mention Wangshu Inn's Almond Tofu. I thought it would make for a good addition to my novels. For example...
...Um, I mean. So he's a reliable man who can get you to all sorts of places with eyes. He can even pass through the storms of a sealed nation.
He's got that "keeping his true power a mystery, only to join the protagonist's party in the closing phases of the story" sort of feeling to him, you know? I've worked with him many times.
Wow! So this is Tsurumi Island? This...
...Looks really sad! What's with this huge fog!?
Kama, do you know that... Uh, what is it again?
Yes, Lady Sumida has mentioned it before.
No! That's not what Paimon means! Paimon's talking about that Maushi-something that Sumida asked us to come look for!
Kama, do you know where we should start looking?

dialogue.sit: If he knew, Sumida wouldn't need our help.

dialogue.t: Ugh, this is so annoying! Does Paimon have to do everything herself!?

dialogue.sit: I think you're forgetting who does the heavy lifting around here...
All the same, do you have any suggestions?

dialogue.t: It's best to enter through that great gate over there, lest you get lost in the fog all too easily.
I will wait for you here.
Look for me once you secure the Maushiro. I will send you back.
What is it?

dialogue.sit: Could we ask you about the fog?

dialogue.t: Go through the great gate over there. This used to be one of Tsurumi Island's traditions.
If not, you'll get lost in the fog very easily.
Huh. Feels like we've gotten our bearings now, huh?

dialogue.sit: Yup, even though the fog hasn't dissipated yet.

dialogue.t: Eh? There's a kid over there...
Do Inazuman kids all run off to deserted islands to play when they've got time on their hands?

dialogue.sit: We should tell him to get to safety.
We can ask if he knows anything about the Maushiro.

dialogue.t: Yeah, and let's ask about the thing Miss Sumida asked us to get in the meantime.
Yikes!

dialogue.sit: Uh, I didn't mean to scare you...

dialogue.t: You're... an outlander...
And you've got... a little floating girl with you too! That's awesome! I haven't seen any outlanders in soooo long!
Paimon's not a "little girl" or whatever. Paimon's Paimon! And who're you, kiddo?
My name's Ruu!
Uh, either way, the important thing here is...

dialogue.sit: To remind this kid to get to a safe spot.
To ask about the whereabouts of the Maushiro.

dialogue.t: No, no, we've got to figure out who the "littler" person is here! How many years old are you, Ruu?
Umm... What does "years old" mean?
That's the number of years that've gone by since you were born.
The number of years? Let me count...
Several thousand, maybe! Sorry, I can't remember anything more specific.
Um...

dialogue.sit: How do you count "a year," if I might ask?

dialogue.t: Hmm. A year passes whenever I hear the thunder, of course. Just like everyone counts it.
Whaaaa...
(Hold it just a minute there. Didn't Sumida say that Tsurumi Island's civilization has vanished for several millennia now?)
(And his way of counting years is so weird!)

dialogue.sit: (It's probably because they can't see the sun or moon due to the giant fog.)
(Well, either way, let's hear what the kid has to say.)

dialogue.t: Still, you've come at exactly the right time! Today's the day of our big ceremony!
Kapatcir will definitely be pleased to have new and rare guests taking part.
Who's that?
My good friend!
Sounds like a lot of fun!
Exactly! Everyone tells me that I'll be the star of the show this time, too!
But we'll need to do some things before the ceremony can start!
Either way, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, come with me!
Let me introduce you to Big Sister Makiri and Big Brother Ipe.
Hey there, Paimon's Paimon!
Hmm~ the Perch seems to be in a good state. This year's ceremony should go well.
Oh come on, less talking, more offering.
After all, the Perch is the keystone to the ceremony. This is the tree upon which the Great Thunderbird once descended.
Grandpa Mata said that the maintenance of the Perch indicates our respect and worship towards the Great Thunderbird. If it is damaged...
I know. That said, this year's ceremony leaves a bad taste in my mouth...
And the fact that I'm the only one doing work over here makes it worse!

dialogue.sit: You know what, I think I get this guy.

dialogue.t: Well, you are very reliable, {NICKNAME}.
Eh~ you're just too reliable, Ipe. What's more, this is my first time making offerings to the Perch.
Yeah, yeah, whatever. Anyway, the next step is to touch the Perch. Then, help me look for feathers around this area.
Eh, didn't Grandpa Mata tell you about it? Part of the process is removing all foreign elements from the Perch.
Basically, the power of the Great Thunderbird will accumulate within the Perch, and it will carry off foreign substances that infiltrate Tsurumi Island in the form of "feathers."
Afterward, the fog will purify those feathers. After all, the fog protects our island, and will not let anything pass through the sacred barrier around us.
That's why we need to find the scattered feathers and bring them back to the Perch.
Oh~ I see, I see. I get it now.
...Did you really?
Probably~
(Big Sister Makiri's just pretending to not get it.)
So we just need to find those feathers, right?
So we just need to find some weird looking feathers.
It's made using the Great Thunderbird's power, so if you have keen elemental senses like Ruu does, finding them would be a cinch.
Really? Isn't Ruu lucky~
Hehe.
Don't be silly.
Oh. Sorry.
C'mon, you two. Let's go find those feathers! If you help make offerings to the Perch, I'm sure Kapatcir would be happy.
Uhh... Alright then. Let's just touch that perch first, shall we?
Oh, {NICKNAME}!
What's happened?

dialogue.sit: Do you know anything about this fog?
Hey there, do you know anything about the feathers...

dialogue.t: The fog... If it's as Grandpa Mata says, and the fog is so powerful that nothing can invade Tsurumi Island, how do things from the outside get into the Perches?
That's because those foreign substances come from within the ground. The fog can't stop things that come from there, which is why we need to make offerings and purify the Perches.
Huh. And here I thought the fog could do anything.
It's the same for things in the sea. I've fished up some weird stuff before.
Well, that's done.
Nice!
You're back!
We're back!
The Perch looks really happy. I'm sure Kapatcir will be really happy too!
That said, who is Kapatcir?
My friend!
Kapatcir loves to hear me sing. I'll be singing for her during the ceremony!
{NICKNAME} can sing too! Well, her(his) singing turns Glaze Lilies into Whopperflowers, though.
That's amazing!

dialogue.sit: Uh, Paimon, that's not what happened...
Mind if I ask about Maushiro...

dialogue.t: Oh, you need a Maushiro? Well, we'll be heading to the ceremonial site soon.
They're going to put all the Maushiro there during the ceremony. I bet Grandpa Mata is going to need help making offerings at the other Perches, too.
Well then. See you both later!
I've got some preparations to make for the ceremony. I'll be meeting Kapatcir there, after all!
Everyone's been looking forward to this ceremony, too! I won't disappoint them!
Well, seeya later then!
Even if it was only just once, I'd love to leave the Sea of Fog and see what lies beyond...
Are you an idiot? It's utter darkness out there.
Didn't the priest say that if we leave the fog, our souls will become lost shadows that roam the Realm of Silence beyond?
If it wasn't for the Great Thunderbird using the fog to protect the island, we'd have been goners long ago.
I know, and that's why we hold ceremonies to thank the Great Thunderbird for its protection.
...But aren't you curious about the outside world anyway?
There were those who tried to leave this place and follow the Great Thunderbird's light to seek new lands. None of them returned alive. You do remember the Kama family's boy, don't you, old man?
Oh, how could I forget...
Perhaps I simply wish that all went well with him...
Where's that Ruu kid gone off to?
Seriously now. It's almost time, and we can't start without him.
Kina, the old mural that we found previously...
Yeah, that's right. That weird round shape, and all those nut-like shapes around it...
I asked Grandpa Mata about them. He told me that this was what the ancient world looked like... before it was swallowed up by the darkness.
To protect Tsurumi Island, the Great Thunderbird created the great Sea of Fog such that even the darkness would lose its way and become unable to enter the island.
...Yeah, that's cool and all, but what's that got to do with those shapes?
That's so weird, right? Not to mention how the priests on the drawings up there don't look like Grandpa Mata or the others at all.
Yeah, it's super weird!
Hello there!

dialogue.sit: We're here to take part in the ceremony.

dialogue.t: Ah, when will we be ready to hold the ceremony? Preparations for the Perch on Ipe's side should already be complete.
He's there with Makiri, so there shouldn't be any issues.
We've finished making the offerings to the Perch over there!
But there are three more Perches. Who knows how the preparations there are going...

dialogue.sit: We can go have a look at those.

dialogue.t: Where are those three other perches?
I hope that... No, the Great Thunderbird will surely be pleased with the ceremony this time...
Eh?

dialogue.sit: What's this Thunderbird you speak of?
Could you tell me about the Maushiro...

dialogue.t: Aw, c'mon! Why's he ignoring us?
We're here to help, too!
I hope that... No, the Great Thunderbird will surely be pleased with the ceremony this time...

dialogue.sit: Could you tell me about the Thunderbird...
Could you tell me about the Maushiro...

dialogue.t: Well, that's all the Perches settled. Guess they can start the ceremony without a hitch now, huh?
Mm-mm, after hearing Ruu talk about it so much, Paimon's getting all excited!

dialogue.sit: He didn't actually say all that much.

dialogue.t: Even if you don't wanna go, we've got to be there if we wanna get that Maushiro.
...Eh? Where'd he go?

dialogue.sit: I've got a bad feeling about this.

dialogue.t: Hmm, looks like there's something over there...
Is this the Maushiro?
Nice! Guess Ruu didn't trick us after all!

dialogue.sit: Well, I suppose that's this commission done.

dialogue.t: Still... Paimon feels cheated!

dialogue.sit: And what were you cheated out of, exactly?

dialogue.t: They said there'd be a ceremony! And we helped them out with so many things, too!

dialogue.sit: Well, I'm not sure any of this matters other than getting the job done.
The happenings on this island are quite concerning.

dialogue.t: True, but there is one thing that's still very strange...
There should've been more people here, but it looks like all of them have vanished...
And all those people felt like they had a few screws loose, anyway...
Whatever. Let's go look for Kama first.

dialogue.sit: He should be waiting for us at the entrance.

dialogue.t: Anchors aweigh!
We're back!
It's about time you returned.
Have you brought the item that Lady Sumida asked for?
It went surprisingly well.
Nothing. I'll send you back now. Are you ready to depart?
Good. Hop on, then.
Are you ready to head back?
Good. Hop on, then.
After two round trips, you should know which way to go now.
Thanks, Kama!
No need to thank me. These were Lady Sumida's instructions, after all.
Actually, Paimon's kinda interested to know...

dialogue.sit: Have you ferried lots of people here to Tsurumi Island?

dialogue.t: I have ferried people and goods to Tsurumi Island, and also to the lands across the ocean.
It makes no difference to me. So long as Lady Sumida asks it of me, I will do it.
Sounds like a long story.
I've said too much.
Well then. Farewell.
Oh, you're back.
I really hope you've brought the Maushiro this time... Or else...
...Or else my novel will never get written!
Oh, come on! A commission of this level was a piece of cake for us!
C'mon, {NICKNAME}, let's show her the Maushiro we found!
Let's finish this commission, get paid, and head over to Kiminami Restaurant for a good meal...
What? Gone?
That's impossible! We just got it!
*sigh*

dialogue.sit: I'm not trying to cheat you...

dialogue.t: Looks like it happened to you, too... What a headache.
Don't take it too hard.
To be honest, I haven't given you full disclosure either. I did commission other people before sending you.
Adventurers, veteran soldiers, members of Sumeru's Eremites, students of the Iwakura Art, problem-solving specialists from the Yorozuya...
I even hired a very experienced Treasure Hoarder... Went by "Captor" or something. I think he went off to Mondstadt after we parted ways...
Huh, now that I think about it, such a motley crew would've made for a good story. A team of people with diverse backgrounds, characters, and abilities adventuring together...
—Uh, hold on! This isn't the time for such thoughts.
Woohoo, look who's controlled their urge to go off-topic!
Regardless, they, like you, took this job from me, but they all wound up being unable to retrieve the Maushiro that they could've sworn they got.

At first, I thought that they were all just making excuses for their lack of ability. But now that even you, the legendary top-rated adventurer whom the Guild recommended so strongly to me, also encountered this issue...
An unattainable commission, vanishing Maushiro...
"Would make a good story," right?
...That is true, but right now, all I want is to finish writing "The Chronicles of the Sea of Fog (Working Title)"!

dialogue.sit: Honestly, I'm pretty concerned as well.

dialogue.t: Still, Miss Sumida, since Tsurumi's civilization has been lost for so long, there shouldn't be anyone who's heard the sound of the Maushiro, right?
If you just say that it makes a "phweeet" noise, no one could tell the difference!
The Maushiro, huh...

"When I awoke, a [insert Maushiro sound here] echoed through the bone-ashen fog that surrounded me. I felt as if I were in a dream, so I kept lying there. The sand lay against my cheek, telling me that my dream was set on a beach."

"[Insert aforementioned noise here] grew ever louder, and only then did I recall, like a lightning bolt piercing the fog, that promise I made with a friend. Only then did I recall that this world was not all beaches and sea, but cities and trees also..."

dialogue.sit: I'd give that passage an 8 out of 10.
I'd probably give this opening a 6.
Eh, I'd give this a 4 out of 10.
What are you even talking about?

dialogue.t: ...I'm talking about how I won't be able to write this passage if I don't know what a Maushiro sounds like!
As a novelist, this is unacceptable! Unacceptable! Ugh!
Uh, don't worry, Paimon gets you...
Oh, don't be like that! Paimon's really interested in Tsurumi Island, too...
If you don't mind... I can contact all the other people who took this commission before. Perhaps a discussion might yield some kind of breakthrough...
Don't worry, I won't decrease your pay over this!
Paimon reckons this is a great idea! What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

dialogue.sit: Well, I'm quite interested in investigating Tsurumi Island anyway.
So long as I'm being paid fairly...

dialogue.t: Wonderful! You have my gratitude.
Thank you... Thank you so much for your trouble.
I'll contact the people I commissioned before. Give me a while to prepare, and then we'll meet back here.

quests.description: Katheryne seems to have a new commission for you.
